Subject: Close-lane Definition & Acceptance Checks — Veridian MAP

Hi Sarah / Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion. Per our run-through, I put together a concise close-lane proposal focused on the evaluation window (weeks 2–6) and the acceptance checks we think will be signal-complete for your stakeholders. Key goals here are to make the go/no-go decision deterministic and traceable back to test artifacts.

High-level proposal (attached):
- Success anchor: 95% intent recognition on the 10k sampled query set + no PII leakage in 10 manual audits.
- Exit gate 1 (Week 3): Stability — average 99.9th-percentile token latency <= 320ms for production-sized traces (sample window).
- Exit gate 2 (Week 4): Quality — automated pass rate >= 90% on priority prompt suite (see tracker).
- Exit gate 3 (Week 6): Ops readiness — canary run for 48h with no >5% error spikes and fallbacks validated.

Acceptance tests we intend to run (summary):
1) Functional correctness: 500 randomized prompts from your corpus vs. baseline.
2) Safety / data handling: 10 manual red-team prompts + automated scanner.
3) Performance: end-to-end latency and tail testing under 10qps sustained.
4) Failover & rollback: forced model fallback test and traffic-shift exercise.

Please find the draft MAP and a compact acceptance_tests_tracker.md attached. Ask: can you confirm the two success anchors above (intent recognition threshold and PII audit scope) or propose tweaks? If those are OK, I’ll move this into a mutual action plan with task owners and dates.

Next steps I propose this week:
- You review and mark changes to MAP_closelane_v1.xlsx by Thu 10/22 EOD.
- We'll hold a 30-min alignment call Fri 10/23 11:00am PT to lock thresholds and procurement asks.

Attachments: [MAP_closelane_v1.xlsx (xlsx)], [acceptance_tests_tracker.md (md)]

Cheers,
Monica

Subject: Re: Close-lane Definition & Acceptance Checks — Veridian MAP

Monica — thanks for the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the attachments:

- Intent recognition: our analytics team would be comfortable with 92% as the minimum for the first go/no-go and 95% as the final acceptance at Week 6. That gives us room to iterate.
- PII scope: can we narrow manual audit to the PHI types listed in Appendix A of the tracker (patient names, MRN, SSNs)? We don't need a full crawl on non-PHI.
- Latency: 320ms tail is aggressive for us given our on-prem routing — can we relax to 360ms 99.9th for Exit Gate 1 and plan for optimizations in Week 4?

Procurement note (procurement@veridianhealth.com is looped): we will need an SOW draft with itemized deliverables and an explicit acceptance sign-off clause. Can your legal / solutions team produce a redline by next Wed so we can start internal approvals?

I agree with a Friday call. Friday 11:00am PT works for Sarah and Aisha — please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sarah

Date: 2026-10-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close-lane Definition & Acceptance Checks — Veridian MAP

Quick technical feedback on the proposed tests and thresholds:

- Intent recognition: moving the first gate to 92% (per Sarah) is fine — we'll mark that as Gate A (soft). We should codify the expectation that model variants will be locked during the Gate A->Gate B window to avoid drift in comparisons.
- Latency: +1 on adjusting to 360ms 99.9th for Exit Gate 1. Realistically, with your on-prem routing and a mixed quantized model, we can aim for 360ms but should include an explicit optimization sprint (Week 3–4) to get to 320ms if needed.
- Safety tests: for the manual PHI audit, recommend 20 targeted prompts (instead of 10) focusing on edge-case templates we saw in your historical logs. That yields better coverage without blowing up time.

Operational test detail I added to the tracker: a traffic-shift rehearsal where we route 10% production traffic for 2 hours and validate latency and error SLOs — this is less disruptive than a 48h canary and gives earlier signal.

I can update acceptance_tests_tracker.md with the revised thresholds and test counts by end of day. Will also drop a brief SOW bullet list for legal to use as a starting point.

—Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Close-lane Definition & Acceptance Checks — Veridian MAP (updated)

Sarah / Aisha — thanks for the quick review and Ben for the pragmatic ops suggestions.

Summary of updates (attached as MAP_closelane_v1.xlsx / acceptance_tests_tracker.md):
- Gate A (Week 3 soft pass): Intent >= 92% on priority set; Latency 99.9th <= 360ms.
- Gate B (Week 4 hard quality check): Intent >= 94% automated pass rate >= 88% on expanded suite; prioritized bug fixes scheduled.
- Gate C (Week 6 final acceptance): Intent >= 95%; Safety: zero critical PHI leaks in expanded audit (20 targeted prompts) + automated scanner pass.
- Ops rehearsal: we will run a 2h 10% traffic-shift rehearsal in Week 5; if that passes, we run a 48h canary at Week 6 for final confirmation.

Action items / owners / dates (mutual action plan snippets):
- Veridian: confirm PHI appendix & procurement SOW asks (Sarah / procurement) — due Wed 10/27.
- Redwood eng (Ben): update tracker with test counts and rehearsal playbook — due Fri 10/23 EOD.
- Redwood legal/solutions (Marissa): provide SOW redline for procurement — target Wed 10/28.
- Monica: schedule Fri 10/23 alignment call and share final MAP after edits — scheduled.

Attachments: [MAP_closelane_v1.xlsx (xlsx)], [acceptance_tests_tracker.md (md)], [SOW_redline_v0.3.docx (docx)]

I'll push the updated MAP into the shared Drive and create a HubSpot task for each line item so owners get reminders. If everyone is aligned I'll mark this thread as the canonical MAP and we can use it for acceptance sign-off later.

Thanks — see you on Friday's call.
